newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rates end down on pre-holiday cover.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rates end down on pre-holiday cover.

text.p: Mexico Cetes rates closed down 55 basis points at 29 percent on Tuesday due to late demand from some dealers seeking to cover short positions.
"Trading was light again. The public holiday tomorrow prompted some to demand paper and try to cover positions before the close," said a trader.
Wednesday sees the Anniversary of the Revolution holiday, and Mexican financial markets will be closed.
Traders said that a stable peso and relatively unchanged primary auction results helped the overnight rate to fluctuate in the 29.00-29.40 percent range during the session.
The benchmark 48-hour peso closed earlier 0.4 of a centavo weaker at 7.8880/7.8940 per dollar.
Banco de Mexico assigned bellwether 28-day rates at 29.85 percent at Monday night's primary auction, just four basis points down on last week's rate.
Bank paper meanwhile closed ten basis points off at 30.80 percent.
The central bank offset liquidity shortages during the session by injecting 4.897 billion dollars through four credit auctions, which it assigned at between 31.54 and 30.95 percent.
Credit maturities for Thursday were estimated at 3.731 billion pesos, and traders said liquidity would be further squeezed by an overplacement of 365 million pesos from the primary auction.
